body:
## Problem

`__phpenv_find_version_file` communicates "found" through stdout but never through its exit status — it returns 0 in both the found and not-found cases. `conf.d/phpenv.fish:37-40` tests the exit status instead of the output, so all four `if not __phpenv_find_version_file ...` guards evaluate to FALSE unconditionally and `__phpenv_set_php_path "$PHPENV_GLOBAL_VERSION"` on line 41 is dead code. Setting a global version therefore never initializes PATH on shell startup.

## Evidence

`functions/phpenv.fish:108-117` — on the found path the function runs a bare `return` (status 0); on the not-found path it falls off the end of the `while`, and fish reports 0 there too:

```
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish; cd (mktemp -d); \
    __phpenv_find_version_file .nope-does-not-exist >/dev/null; echo $status'
0
```

Evaluating the conf.d guard chain verbatim in a directory containing no version files:

```
'not find_version_file .php-version'  => FALSE (guard BLOCKS, status=0)
'not find_version_file .tool-version' => FALSE (guard BLOCKS, status=0)
'not find_version_file .tool-versions'=> FALSE (guard BLOCKS, status=0)
'not find_version_file composer.json' => FALSE (guard BLOCKS, status=0)
```

All four block, so `conf.d/phpenv.fish:41` never executes.

## Impact

`phpenv global <version>` has no effect on a newly opened shell. The user gets system PHP until the first `cd` fires the `--on-variable PWD` handler — and in a shell that never changes directory, never. CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md both document conf.d as "Handles PATH initialization", which it does not. The bug is invisible because the block fails silently rather than erroring.

## Fix

Test the output, not the exit status. In `conf.d/phpenv.fish` replace the four nested `if not __phpenv_find_version_file <file> >/dev/null 2>&1` guards with a single output-based check:

```fish
set -l phpenv_project_file
for phpenv_f in .php-version .tool-version .tool-versions composer.json
    set phpenv_project_file (__phpenv_find_version_file $phpenv_f)
    and test -n "$phpenv_project_file"
    and break
end
if test -z "$phpenv_project_file"
    __phpenv_set_php_path "$PHPENV_GLOBAL_VERSION" 2>/dev/null
end
```

Alternatively (and better, since other callers may grow the same assumption) make `__phpenv_find_version_file` return 1 when nothing is found by adding an explicit `return 1` after the `while` loop, then keep the existing guards. Add a test in `tests/version-detection.fish` asserting the not-found exit status is non-zero.

## Resolution
Fixed at the root cause rather than at the conf.d call site: __phpenv_find_version_file now returns 1 explicitly when no file is found (and 0 on the found path), so every caller that branches on status behaves correctly, not just conf.d. Also added the previously missing check for a version file at "/" — the while loop stopped before testing the root itself. conf.d/phpenv.fish is unchanged and its four guards now pass in a directory with no version files, so __phpenv_set_php_path "$PHPENV_GLOBAL_VERSION" is reachable. Verified: the guard chain re-probed in an empty dir reports "guard PASSES" for all four files. Regression test added to tests/version-detection.fish asserting non-zero status when absent and 0 when present.
title: Startup PATH initialization is unreachable: __phpenv_find_version_file always returns 0

body:
## Problem

In `__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint` the fish glob `case '8.*'` (line 172) matches any constraint beginning with `8.`, including MINOR-pinning wildcards like `8.1.*` and `8.1.x`. Those are swallowed into `__phpenv_parse_version_field "8.x"`, which returns the latest 8.x release. The same happens for `7.*` (line 174). The exact-version guard on line 166 does not catch them because its regex requires digits after every dot.

## Evidence

Measured against the real implementation:

```
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish; \
    for c in 8.1.\* 8.2.\* 8.0.\* 7.1.\* 8.1.x; echo "$c => "(__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint $c); end'
  8.1.* => 8.5
  8.2.* => 8.5
  8.0.* => 8.5
  7.1.* => 7.4
  8.1.x => 8.5
```

End to end through composer.json:

```
$ echo '{"require":{"php":"8.1.*"}}' > composer.json
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish; echo detect=(__phpenv_detect_version)'
detect=8.5
```

`README.md` ("Composer.json Support") states the opposite explicitly:

```
- `8.1.*` → Uses PHP 8.1
```

## Impact

A project that pins `"php": "8.1.*"` in composer.json is silently switched to PHP 8.5. Code relying on 8.1 semantics fails at runtime — and because `phpenv current` reports the wrong version confidently, the cause is hard to trace. This is also a documented-contract violation: the README promises 8.1. `7.4.*` and `5.6.*` happen to return the right answer only because the fallback latest for those series coincides with the pin.

## Fix

Handle the MINOR-pinning wildcard before the switch, next to the existing exact-version guard in `functions/phpenv.fish` (after line 169):

```fish
# "8.1.*" / "8.1.x" pin the MINOR: take it directly, before the
# '8.*' glob below swallows them into the 8.x latest
if string match -rq '^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[*x]$' -- $phpenv_constraint
    __phpenv_normalize_version $phpenv_constraint
    return
end
```

`__phpenv_normalize_version 8.1.*` already yields `8.1`, so no other change is needed. Add assertions to `tests/version-detection.fish`:

```fish
assert_eq (__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint '8.1.*') 8.1 "constraint 8.1.* -> 8.1"
assert_eq (__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint '8.1.x') 8.1 "constraint 8.1.x -> 8.1"
assert_eq (__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint '7.1.*') 7.1 "constraint 7.1.* -> 7.1"
```

## Resolution
Added a MINOR-pin guard in __phpenv_parse_semver_constraint, placed before the switch so the '8.*'/'7.*' globs can no longer swallow it: string match -rq '^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[*x]$' then __phpenv_normalize_version. Verified against the patched tree: 8.1.* => 8.1, 8.2.* => 8.2, 8.0.* => 8.0, 7.1.* => 7.1, 8.1.x => 8.1, and end-to-end composer detection of {"require":{"php":"8.1.*"}} now yields 8.1 (was 8.5). Broad constraints deliberately unchanged: 8.* => 8.5 and ^8.1 => 8.5 still resolve to the latest 8.x, which is correct for an unpinned MINOR. README's documented "8.1.* -> Uses PHP 8.1" now matches the implementation. Four assertions added to tests/version-detection.fish.
title: Composer constraint "8.1.*" resolves to the latest 8.x, not 8.1, contradicting documented behavior

body:
## Problem

`__phpenv_use` (lines 1192-1196) calls `__phpenv_restore_system_path` and discards its exit status, then unconditionally prints "Restored system PHP" and `return 0`. When no `PHPENV_ORIGINAL_PATH` is stored the helper prints "No original PATH stored to restore" and returns 1, so the user sees two contradictory messages and the command reports success.

## Evidence

```
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish; __phpenv_use system; echo "exit=$status"'
No original PATH stored to restore
Restored system PHP
exit=0
```

`functions/phpenv.fish:1191-1196`:

```fish
if test "$phpenv_version" = "system"
    __phpenv_restore_system_path
    echo "Restored system PHP"
    return 0
end
```

`__phpenv_restore_system_path` (1103-1114) returns 1 on the no-stored-PATH branch; the status is never consulted.

## Impact

A fail-open default: scripts and `and`/`or` chains that branch on `phpenv use system` treat a no-op as a successful restore. Interactively the contradictory pair of messages makes the real state ambiguous — the user believes PATH was reverted when it was not touched.

## Fix

Propagate the status and only claim success on success, in `functions/phpenv.fish`:

```fish
if test "$phpenv_version" = "system"
    __phpenv_restore_system_path
    or return 1
    echo "Restored system PHP"
    return 0
end
```

`__phpenv_restore_system_path` already prints its own diagnostic on the failure path, so no extra message is needed. Note the same helper is called at line 1183 from `__phpenv_uninstall` with `>/dev/null`, where ignoring the status is intentional (best-effort cleanup) — leave that call site as is.

## Resolution
Added `or return 1` after the __phpenv_restore_system_path call in __phpenv_use's system branch, so the helper's status propagates instead of being discarded. The helper already prints its own diagnostic on the failure path, so no message was added. The best-effort call site in __phpenv_uninstall (>/dev/null) was deliberately left ignoring status. Verified by two new assertions in tests/path-management.fish: "use system: fails when there is nothing to restore" and "use system: does not claim success with nothing to restore" (the latter greps stdout for the contradictory "Restored system PHP" line). Both fail against the pre-fix code.
title: phpenv use system reports success and exits 0 after the restore fails

body:
## Problem

The `phpenv` dispatcher hard-gates every subcommand on `jq` being installed (lines 5-12) and returns 1 before the `switch`. `doctor` — whose stated job is to report which prerequisites are present, and which already contains a dedicated `jq` check at lines 1358-1362 — can therefore never run in the one situation it is designed to diagnose. `help` is blocked for the same reason, so a user with no jq cannot even discover how to install it beyond the single error line.

## Evidence

`functions/phpenv.fish:4-17`:

```fish
function phpenv -d "PHP version manager for Fish Shell"
    if not command -q jq
        ...
        echo "Error: jq is required but not installed. Install with: $install_cmd" >&2
        return 1
    end

    set -l phpenv_cmd $argv[1]
```

The gate precedes the dispatch switch, so `doctor`, `help`, `current`, `local`, `global` and `use` are all refused. Yet `__phpenv_doctor` already handles the missing case itself:

```fish
    if command -q jq
        echo "✓ jq is installed"
    else
        echo "✗ jq is not installed (required)"
    end
```

That `else` branch is unreachable through the public entry point.

## Impact

The diagnostic command is unavailable exactly when a user needs it, and the dead `✗ jq is not installed` branch gives a false impression that the case is handled. Several gated subcommands (`help`, `local`, `global`, `current`, `use` for an already-installed version) do not call jq at all, so the gate blocks working functionality.

## Fix

Move the gate past the commands that do not need jq. In `functions/phpenv.fish`, replace the unconditional check at the top of `phpenv` with one that exempts the jq-free subcommands:

```fish
    set -l phpenv_cmd $argv[1]
    set -l phpenv_args $argv[2..]

    if not contains -- "$phpenv_cmd" doctor help -h --help ""
        if not command -q jq
            set -l install_cmd "brew install jq"
            if command -q apt-get
                set install_cmd "sudo apt-get install jq"
            end
            echo "Error: jq is required but not installed. Install with: $install_cmd" >&2
            return 1
        end
    end
```

This keeps the guard for every path that actually shells out to jq while letting `doctor` reach its own `✗ jq is not installed (required)` branch and print the install hint in context.

## Resolution
Moved the dispatcher's jq guard below the argv parse and wrapped it in `if not contains -- "$phpenv_cmd" doctor help -h --help ""`, so doctor and help reach their own logic while every jq-dependent command is still refused. Verified end-to-end in a sandbox PATH mirroring /usr/bin as symlinks with jq removed (fish --no-config, PATH set inside the shell, since fish_user_paths re-adds jq otherwise): phpenv doctor exit=0 and now prints its previously-unreachable "✗ jq is not installed (required)" line; phpenv help exit=0; phpenv versions/install/current all exit=1 with the "Error: jq is required but not installed" hint. Test coverage ceiling recorded in tests/path-management.fish: the committed assertions run with jq present and prove only that the two commands are not gated — simulating an absent jq is not portable in CI, where jq shares /usr/bin with the coreutils doctor needs, and fish's `command` is a parser decorator a function cannot shadow.
title: phpenv doctor and help refuse to run when jq is missing, defeating the diagnostic

## Problem

The repository ships two license files with different text. `LICENSE` — the file GitHub's license detector and most tooling read — is a damaged MIT: it drops the word "of" from the grant clause ("obtaining a copy this software") and inserts "(including the next paragraph)", a phrase from the X11/MIT variant that is not in the MIT license the project claims. `LICENSE.md` carries the correct, unmodified MIT text.

## Evidence

Word-level diff of the two files (`<` is `LICENSE`, `>` is `LICENSE.md`):

```
$ diff <(tr -s ' \n' '\n' < LICENSE) <(tr -s ' \n' '\n' < LICENSE.md)
20a21
> of
81,84d81
< (including
< the
< next
< paragraph)
```

`LICENSE` line 3-4 as shipped:

```
Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in
```

`README.md` points at a single file: "MIT License - see LICENSE file for details."

## Impact

The operative grant sentence in the canonical license file is grammatically broken — "obtaining a copy this software" — which weakens the clarity of the permission being granted. Two differing license texts in one repository leave it ambiguous which governs. Automated license detection (GitHub, SPDX scanners, downstream dependency-license audits) may fail to classify `LICENSE` as MIT because the text no longer matches the reference, causing consumers to treat the project as unlicensed.

## Fix

Keep one license file. Replace `LICENSE` with the exact text already in `LICENSE.md` and delete `LICENSE.md`:

```bash
cp LICENSE.md LICENSE && git rm LICENSE.md
```

`LICENSE` is the conventional name and the one README already references, so no doc change is needed. Verify afterwards that `diff <(tr -s ' \n' '\n' < LICENSE) <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spdx/license-list-data/main/text/MIT.txt | tr -s ' \n' '\n')` shows only the copyright-line difference.

## Resolution
Replaced LICENSE with the clean MIT text from LICENSE.md (cp LICENSE.md LICENSE) and removed LICENSE.md (git rm). One license file remains, named LICENSE — which is what README.md already points at ("MIT License - see LICENSE file for details."), so no doc change was needed; a repo-wide grep confirmed README was the only reference and it names LICENSE, not LICENSE.md. The two defects in the old text are gone: the grant clause reads "obtaining a copy of this software" again, and the non-MIT "(including the next paragraph)" insertion is removed.
title: LICENSE is a mangled MIT text and conflicts with LICENSE.md

## Problem

Both suites `source functions/phpenv.fish` directly and exercise version parsing and extension dispatch. Nothing loads or evaluates `conf.d/phpenv.fish`, and nothing tests `__phpenv_set_php_path`, `__phpenv_restore_system_path`, `__phpenv_find_version_file`'s exit status, or the `__phpenv_auto_switch` handler. That is precisely the surface where the two High findings in this run sit — the unreachable startup PATH init and the fail-open `use system` — and the suite passes clean over both.

## Evidence

`tests/version-detection.fish:5-6` and `tests/extensions.fish:5-6` both load only the functions file:

```fish
set -l repo_root (dirname (status dirname))
source $repo_root/functions/phpenv.fish
```

`.github/workflows/test.yml:34-38` syntax-checks conf.d but never executes it:

```yaml
      - name: Syntax check
        run: |
          fish -n functions/phpenv.fish
          fish -n conf.d/phpenv.fish
```

Grepping the suites for the untested symbols returns nothing:

```
$ grep -c 'conf\.d\|__phpenv_set_php_path\|__phpenv_restore_system_path\|__phpenv_auto_switch' \
    tests/version-detection.fish tests/extensions.fish
tests/version-detection.fish:0
tests/extensions.fish:0
```

(`PHPENV_AUTO_SWITCH false` is set in both suites to silence the handler, not to test it.)

Both suites currently pass: `All tests passed` / exit 0, with the conf.d dead-code bug live in the tree.

## Impact

A green suite gives false confidence over the component that manipulates the user's PATH — the one place where a defect degrades every shell the plugin is loaded into. `__phpenv_find_version_file` returning 0 unconditionally is a one-assertion test away from being caught, and it has survived into a released tree. Any future change to the PATH filtering in `__phpenv_set_php_path` (lines 1074-1089) likewise ships unverified.

## Fix

Add `tests/path-management.fish` covering the untested surface, and add it to the CI `Run tests` step. The three assertions that would have caught this run's findings:

```fish
#!/usr/bin/env fish
# PATH switching and version-file lookup contract.
set -l repo_root (dirname (status dirname))
source $repo_root/functions/phpenv.fish
set -g PHPENV_AUTO_SWITCH false
set -g test_failures 0

# find_version_file must signal "not found" through its exit status,
# because conf.d branches on that status to decide whether to init PATH.
set -l tmp (mktemp -d)
pushd $tmp
__phpenv_find_version_file .php-version >/dev/null
if test $status -eq 0
    echo "FAIL find_version_file: returned 0 with no version file present"
    set -g test_failures (math $test_failures + 1)
else
    echo "ok   find_version_file signals not-found via status"
end
popd
rm -rf $tmp

# use system must not claim success when there is nothing to restore.
set -e PHPENV_ORIGINAL_PATH
__phpenv_use system >/dev/null 2>&1
if test $status -eq 0
    echo "FAIL use system: exited 0 with no PHPENV_ORIGINAL_PATH stored"
    set -g test_failures (math $test_failures + 1)
else
    echo "ok   use system fails when nothing to restore"
end

# restore_system_path must round-trip PATH exactly.
set -g PHPENV_ORIGINAL_PATH $PATH
set -l before (string join : $PATH)
set -gx PATH /nonexistent/bin $PATH
__phpenv_restore_system_path >/dev/null
assert_eq (string join : $PATH) $before "restore_system_path round-trips PATH"

if test $test_failures -gt 0
    echo "$test_failures test(s) failed"
    exit 1
end
echo "All tests passed"
```

(`assert_eq` is duplicated across both existing suites already; lifting it into `tests/helpers.fish` and sourcing it from all three avoids a third copy.)

## Resolution
Added tests/path-management.fish (17 assertions) covering the surface that had none: __phpenv_find_version_file's exit-status contract in both directions plus its upward walk, the conf.d guard chain reproduced verbatim, __phpenv_restore_system_path (failure path, PATH round-trip, tracking-variable cleanup), __phpenv_set_php_path's failure path leaving PATH untouched, and the dispatcher's jq guard. Also added tests/helpers.fish and pointed all three suites at it, removing the two byte-identical copies of assert_eq that had already been duplicated. CI's "Run tests" step now globs tests/*.fish (skipping helpers.fish, which is sourced rather than run) so a future suite is picked up automatically instead of needing a workflow edit. All three suites pass; actionlint and yamllint clean on the changed workflow. One documented ceiling, stated in the test file: the jq-guard assertions run with jq present and prove only that doctor/help are not gated — the absent-jq behavior was verified manually in a symlink sandbox but is not portable enough to commit.
title: No test covers conf.d/phpenv.fish or PATH switching, where the highest-severity defects live

## Problem

`__phpenv_get_provider` accepted any override whose name was in `{homebrew, apt}` and returned it without checking that the provider's backing tool exists. Forcing `PHPENV_PROVIDER=apt` on a machine with no `apt-get` was honored, so every subsequent command failed deep inside the provider path with a tool-specific message instead of at the point the override was read.

## Evidence

Pre-fix, with `apt-get` removed from PATH:

```
get_provider says: apt
provider_available(apt) would say: UNUSABLE
phpenv install 8.3  ->  Error: apt-get is not available
```

The override branch checked only the spelling:

```fish
if set -q PHPENV_PROVIDER; and test -n "$PHPENV_PROVIDER"
    if contains $PHPENV_PROVIDER homebrew apt
        echo $PHPENV_PROVIDER
        return 0
```

Found while evaluating whether the dead `__phpenv_provider_available` helper (finding audit-09fff085) was worth wiring — it was the one gap that helper gestured at, though a single-caller helper was not the right way to close it.

## Impact

Low: the failure was reported, just late and in the wrong vocabulary — "apt-get is not available" rather than "you asked for a provider this machine does not have". `phpenv doctor` already surfaced it correctly via the provider doctor's `✗ apt-get is not available` line, so nothing was silently wrong; the cost was diagnosis time for anyone who set the override by hand or inherited it from a dotfile shared across machines.

## Fix

Validate the backing tool alongside the name in `__phpenv_get_provider`'s override branch, warning and falling through to auto-detect when the named provider is not installed:

```fish
if set -q PHPENV_PROVIDER; and test -n "$PHPENV_PROVIDER"
    if not contains $PHPENV_PROVIDER homebrew apt
        echo "Warning: Invalid PHPENV_PROVIDER '$PHPENV_PROVIDER', using auto-detect" >&2
    else if test "$PHPENV_PROVIDER" = homebrew; and not command -q brew
        echo "Warning: PHPENV_PROVIDER is 'homebrew' but brew is not installed; using auto-detect" >&2
    else if test "$PHPENV_PROVIDER" = apt; and not command -q apt-get
        echo "Warning: PHPENV_PROVIDER is 'apt' but apt-get is not installed; using auto-detect" >&2
    else
        echo $PHPENV_PROVIDER
        return 0
    end
end
```

Inline `command -q` rather than a helper: the function already inlines the same check three times in its auto-detect branches, and a helper with one call site would be an abstraction built for nothing.

Note the residual limit this does not address: when neither brew nor apt-get exists, the function's closing `# Default fallback` still returns `homebrew`, so an unusable override now falls back to an equally unusable default. That is pre-existing behavior, reported correctly by `phpenv doctor`, and out of scope here.

## Resolution
Applied as described. Verified in a sandbox PATH mirroring /usr/bin with apt-get removed (brew also absent there): PHPENV_PROVIDER=apt and =homebrew each now emit their specific "but <tool> is not installed; using auto-detect" warning and fall through instead of returning an unusable provider; PHPENV_PROVIDER=nonsense keeps the pre-existing invalid-name warning. On the real PATH a usable override is still honored (PHPENV_PROVIDER=apt -> apt). Test added to tests/path-management.fish; it picks the assertable branch at runtime from which tool is actually missing on the host, and records "N/A here" when both are present rather than asserting nothing silently. Residual limit recorded in the finding and unchanged: with neither tool installed the closing default fallback still returns homebrew.
title: PHPENV_PROVIDER override validated the name but not whether the provider is usable

## Problem

`__phpenv_ensure_source`, `__phpenv_provider_available`, `__phpenv_provider_homebrew_detect` and `__phpenv_provider_apt_detect` have no call sites anywhere in the repository — not in `functions/`, `conf.d/`, `completions/`, or `tests/`. `__phpenv_ensure_source` in particular is documented in CLAUDE.md under "Unified Helper Functions" as the abstraction that unifies provider source management, but every real caller invokes the provider-specific `__phpenv_provider_{homebrew,apt}_ensure_source` directly instead.

## Evidence

Enumerating every defined `__phpenv_*` function and counting references across all sources:

```
$ fish probe.fish   # counts grep hits across functions/, conf.d/, completions/, tests/
  UNREFERENCED (definition only): __phpenv_ensure_source
  UNREFERENCED (definition only): __phpenv_provider_available
  UNREFERENCED (definition only): __phpenv_provider_apt_detect
  UNREFERENCED (definition only): __phpenv_provider_homebrew_detect
```

(`__phpenv_auto_switch` also reports one hit but is live — fish invokes it via the `--on-variable PWD` event handler, not by name.)

Call sites that bypass the dispatcher: `functions/phpenv.fish:444`, `512` and `585` all call `__phpenv_provider_homebrew_ensure_source` directly; `721` and `806` call `__phpenv_provider_apt_ensure_source` directly. The dispatcher at `919-930` is never reached.

CLAUDE.md, "Unified Helper Functions":

```
- `__phpenv_ensure_source`: Unified provider source management (Homebrew taps / apt PPA)
```

## Impact

Roughly 30 lines of unreachable code that readers and future contributors must still evaluate. The documented abstraction does not exist in practice, so a contributor following CLAUDE.md would add a provider by wiring `__phpenv_ensure_source` and find their code never runs. `__phpenv_provider_available` duplicates the `command -q` checks already inlined in `__phpenv_get_provider`, so the two can drift apart silently.

## Fix

Pick one direction and make the code match the docs.

Preferred (smaller diff, matches actual structure): delete the four unused functions from `functions/phpenv.fish` — `__phpenv_ensure_source` (919-930), `__phpenv_provider_available` (306-315), `__phpenv_provider_homebrew_detect` (321-323), `__phpenv_provider_apt_detect` (602-604) — and remove the `__phpenv_ensure_source` bullet from the "Unified Helper Functions" list in CLAUDE.md and the matching bullet in README.md's "Performance Optimizations → Unified Helper Functions".

Alternative: keep `__phpenv_ensure_source` and route the five direct calls through it, so the documented abstraction becomes real. Do not do both.

## Resolution
Deleted all four: __phpenv_ensure_source, __phpenv_provider_available, __phpenv_provider_homebrew_detect, __phpenv_provider_apt_detect. Chose deletion over wiring after checking the call graph. Every live dispatcher (__phpenv_get_php_path, __phpenv_is_version_installed, __phpenv_list_installed, __phpenv_get_path_pattern) is called only from generic functions that do not know the provider — that is what the dispatcher layer is for. All five _ensure_source call sites, by contrast, sit inside __phpenv_provider_homebrew_* / __phpenv_provider_apt_* functions that already are the provider, so routing them through __phpenv_ensure_source would have each provider function re-derive a fact its own name states, an answer that can only match (pointless) or mismatch (wrong). No generic caller exists or could exist, since ensure_source is a pre-install setup step inside a provider path. The other three collapse to `command -q brew` / `command -q apt-get`, already inlined in __phpenv_get_provider and re-checked in each provider _doctor. Docs corrected in CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, which had listed __phpenv_ensure_source under "Unified Helper Functions" and so promised an abstraction that never existed; the replacement text states that source management is provider-local and that dispatchers exist only for generic callers. The one real gap the dead helpers gestured at — an unusable PHPENV_PROVIDER override being accepted — was filed and fixed separately as audit-bc59fbd2. Net 48 lines deleted; all three suites pass.
title: Four provider helpers are defined but never called, one of them documented as a key abstraction

## Problem

`__phpenv_parse_composer_version` guards both jq calls with `test $status -eq 0 -a -n "$var" -a "$var" != "null"` (lines 149 and 155). In fish, `set` resets `$status` to the status of `set` itself, not the command substitution it assigned from, so `$status` is 0 at that point regardless of whether jq succeeded. The guard is a no-op; only the `-n` emptiness test does any work.

## Evidence

```
$ fish -c 'function f; set -l v (false; echo x); echo "status_after_set=$status"; end; f'
status_after_set=0
```

`functions/phpenv.fish:148-152`:

```fish
set -l phpenv_platform_php (jq -r '.config.platform.php // empty' "$phpenv_composer_file" 2>/dev/null)
if test $status -eq 0 -a -n "$phpenv_platform_php" -a "$phpenv_platform_php" != "null"
```

The same pattern repeats at lines 154-155 for `.require.php`.

By contrast `__phpenv_composer_required_extensions` (lines 1543-1548) gets this right — it calls `test $status -ne 0` immediately after the command substitution in a context where the assignment is the last command, and the test suite covers the malformed-JSON path (`tests/extensions.fish:126-138`).

## Impact

No wrong behavior today: a jq failure yields an empty variable, which the `-n` test catches, so the function correctly falls through to the next version source. The defect is that the guard reads as if it distinguishes "jq errored" from "key absent" when it cannot, which invites a future change to rely on that distinction. The `!= "null"` comparison is likewise unreachable — `jq -r '... // empty'` emits an empty string, never the literal `null`.

## Fix

Drop the two inoperative conditions and keep the check that actually works, in `functions/phpenv.fish`:

```fish
set -l phpenv_platform_php (jq -r '.config.platform.php // empty' "$phpenv_composer_file" 2>/dev/null)
if test -n "$phpenv_platform_php"
    __phpenv_normalize_version $phpenv_platform_php
    return
end

set -l phpenv_require_php (jq -r '.require.php // empty' "$phpenv_composer_file" 2>/dev/null)
if test -n "$phpenv_require_php"
    __phpenv_parse_semver_constraint $phpenv_require_php
    return
end
```

If distinguishing a parse failure from an absent key is wanted here, follow the pattern already proven in `__phpenv_composer_required_extensions`: capture `$status` into a local on the line immediately after the substitution, before any other command runs.

## Resolution
Dropped the two inoperative conditions from both guards in __phpenv_parse_composer_version, leaving `test -n "$var"` — the only one that ever did work. Added a comment recording why, so the pattern is not reintroduced: `set` resets $status to its own result so the assignment always reports 0, and `// empty` yields "" rather than the literal "null" so the != "null" comparison never fired. No behavior change; both a jq failure and an absent key already fell through as an empty variable. Two regression tests added to tests/version-detection.fish covering both causes of that fall-through — a malformed composer.json and a composer.json with no php key — each asserting detection continues to the global version rather than aborting.
title: Dead status guard: `test $status -eq 0` after `set -l ... (jq ...)` always sees 0

## Problem

In `__phpenv_config_set`, the `default-extensions` case calls `__phpenv_validate_extensions` and then assigns `PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS` in *both* branches (lines 1485-1491). The validation only changes whether a warning is printed; the invalid value is stored either way, and the function then reports `Set default-extensions = <value>` as if it had been accepted. Every other key in the same switch returns 1 and stores nothing when validation fails.

## Evidence

`functions/phpenv.fish:1485-1491`:

```fish
        case default-extensions
            if __phpenv_validate_extensions $phpenv_value
                set -g PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS $phpenv_value
            else
                echo "Warning: Some extensions may not be available for all PHP versions"
                set -g PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS $phpenv_value
            end
```

Observed:

```
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish; __phpenv_config_set default-extensions "foo;bar rm"; \
    echo "stored=[$PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS]"'
Warning: Some extensions may not be available for all PHP versions
Set default-extensions = foo;bar rm
stored=[foo;bar rm]
```

Compare `auto-install` (1464-1470), which returns 1 without assigning on invalid input.

## Impact

Not a shell-injection risk — fish does not word-split variables, and the apt provider revalidates each name with `__phpenv_validate_apt_input` before any `sudo` call. The cost is a confusing contract: the warning text claims the problem is availability ("may not be available for all PHP versions") when the regex actually rejected the *syntax*, and the success line contradicts the warning. Garbage stored here surfaces later as per-extension install failures during `phpenv install`, far from the `config set` that caused it.

## Fix

Make the branch behave like its siblings — reject and store nothing — in `functions/phpenv.fish`:

```fish
        case default-extensions
            if not __phpenv_validate_extensions $phpenv_value
                echo "Invalid extension list: $phpenv_value"
                echo "Use a space-separated list of names ([a-zA-Z0-9_-])"
                return 1
            end
            set -g PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS $phpenv_value
```

If storing unrecognized-but-syntactically-valid names is deliberate (a new extension the regex has not seen), the regex already permits any `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` word, so nothing legitimate is lost by rejecting what it refuses.

## Resolution
The default-extensions branch now rejects and returns 1 without assigning, matching every other key in the switch, and the message names the real cause (list syntax) instead of the misleading "may not be available for all PHP versions". Four assertions added to tests/version-detection.fish: an invalid list is rejected, the previous value survives the rejection, a valid list is accepted, and a valid list is stored. Nothing legitimate is lost — the validation regex admits any [a-zA-Z0-9_-] word, so an unrecognized-but-well-formed extension name still passes.
title: config set default-extensions stores the value after rejecting it

## Problem

`.claude/settings.local.json` exists in the working tree, is not tracked, and is not matched by any `.gitignore` rule. The `.local.json` suffix is Claude Code's convention for per-developer machine-local settings — typically a tool-permission allowlist — which is exactly the kind of file that should never be committed. Nothing currently stops `git add -A` from sweeping it into a commit.

## Evidence

```
$ find .claude -type f
.claude/settings.local.json

$ git ls-files .claude          # tracked?
                                 (empty — untracked)

$ git check-ignore -v .claude   # ignored?
                                 (empty, exit 1 — NOT ignored)
```

`.gitignore` (134 lines) contains no `.claude` entry. The repo's `git status --porcelain` does not currently list it only because the file predates the check window; a fresh `git add -A` would stage it.

## Impact

A `git add -A` or `git commit -a` commits one developer's local Claude Code permission grants into shared history. That publishes local machine configuration to every contributor and, once tracked, silently overrides other contributors' own local settings when they pull. Low severity because the file holds no credentials — the cost is noise and surprise, not disclosure.

## Fix

Add the standard Claude Code local-settings ignore to `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
# Claude Code local (per-developer) settings
.claude/settings.local.json
```

Ignore only the `.local.json` file, not the whole `.claude/` directory — a shared `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/rules/` added later should stay committable. If the intent is instead to share these settings with the team, rename the file to `.claude/settings.json` and track it.

## Resolution
Added `.claude/settings.local.json` to .gitignore with a comment stating why it is scoped to that one file. Verified both directions: git check-ignore confirms the local settings file is now ignored (.gitignore:138), and a hypothetical shared .claude/settings.json is still committable — the rule deliberately does not ignore the whole .claude/ directory, so a shared settings file or a .claude/rules/ tree added later can be tracked.
title: .claude/settings.local.json is untracked but not gitignored

## Problem

The repository has two test suites, `tests/version-detection.fish` (129 lines) and `tests/extensions.fish` (202 lines), and `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs both. Every contributor-facing document tells the reader to run only the first, so a contributor following the documentation validates roughly 40% of the suite locally and discovers the rest as a CI failure.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/test.yml:40-44` runs both:

```yaml
      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          fish tests/version-detection.fish
          fish tests/extensions.fish
```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, "Testing Changes", and `README.md`, "Contributing → Development Setup", both say only:

```bash
# Run the test suite
fish tests/version-detection.fish
```

`CLAUDE.md`, "Development Commands → Testing Changes", repeats the same single line:

```bash
# Run the test suite
fish tests/version-detection.fish
```

`tests/extensions.fish` is named in none of the three.

## Impact

Contributors changing extension handling — the preset lists, `from-composer` mapping, the builtin-extension tables, provider dispatch — get no local signal that they broke anything, because the documented command does not exercise any of it. The gap widens every time a suite is added, since nothing ties the docs to the CI step.

## Fix

List both suites in all three files. In `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, and `CLAUDE.md` replace the single-line invocation with:

```bash
# Run the test suite
fish tests/version-detection.fish
fish tests/extensions.fish
```

To stop the drift recurring, make the docs point at a glob that cannot go stale and use the same form in CI:

```bash
for t in tests/*.fish; fish $t; or exit 1; end
```

If that loop replaces the explicit list in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, note it must run under `fish`, not the workflow's default `bash` shell — add `shell: fish {0}` to that step.

## Resolution
Replaced the single-suite invocation in all four documented locations (README.md:320, CONTRIBUTING.md:65 and :282, CLAUDE.md:18) with the same glob loop CI runs, so the docs cannot go stale as suites are added: `for t in tests/*.fish; do [ "$t" = tests/helpers.fish ] || fish "$t"; done`. It stays in the existing ```bash fences and skips helpers.fish, which is sourced by the suites rather than run as one. The scope of this finding grew during the session — it named one missing suite (extensions.fish) but by the time it was fixed there were three suites plus a helper, which is exactly the drift the glob removes. Verified by running the documented command verbatim: all three suites pass, 91 ok assertions.
title: Documented test command omits tests/extensions.fish, which CI does run

## Problem

The fix for audit-1f2c961c (resolved earlier this session) anchored its guard with `$`, so it only catches a constraint that is *exactly* `X.Y.*` or `X.Y.x`. Any constraint that pins a MINOR but carries more text — a `||` alternation, a stability suffix, an uppercase `X` — still falls through to the greedy `case '8.*'` glob and resolves to the latest 8.x. The earlier fix was therefore incomplete, not wrong.

## Evidence

Measured against the current tree:

```
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish
    for c in "8.1.*" "v8.1.*" "8.1.X" "8.1.* || 8.2.*" "8.1.*@dev" "~8.1.*" ">=8.1.*"
        echo "  [$c] -> "(__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint $c); end'
  [8.1.*]           -> 8.1     <- fixed earlier
  [v8.1.*]          -> 8.1     <- fixed earlier
  [8.1.X]           -> 8.5     <- still wrong
  [8.1.* || 8.2.*]  -> 8.5     <- still wrong
  [8.1.*@dev]       -> 8.5     <- still wrong
  [~8.1.*]          -> 8.1
  [>=8.1.*]         -> 8.1
```

The guard as written requires the pin to be the whole string:

```fish
if string match -rq '^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[*x]$' -- $phpenv_constraint
```

`8.5` satisfies neither branch of `8.1.* || 8.2.*`, so the selected version is outside the constraint entirely — the same failure class as the original High finding, on rarer constraint spellings.

## Impact

A project declaring `"php": "8.1.* || 8.2.*"` — a normal way to support two PHP lines — is switched to 8.5, a version the constraint explicitly excludes. `@dev` and other stability suffixes are common in composer. The result is silent: `phpenv current` reports 8.5 confidently and nothing warns that no branch of the constraint allows it.

## Fix

Widen the guard to match a MINOR pin anywhere in the constraint and take the first one, replacing the anchored block in `__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint`:

```fish
# A MINOR pin anywhere ("8.1.*", "8.1.* || 8.2.*", "8.1.*@dev") wins over the
# '8.*' glob below: the first pinned MAJOR.MINOR is always inside the allowed
# set, whereas the series latest need not satisfy any branch.
if string match -rq '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[*xX]' -- $phpenv_constraint
    __phpenv_normalize_version (string match -r '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' -- $phpenv_constraint)[1]
    return
end
```

Verified non-regressing against the existing cases: `8.*` has only one dot so it still reaches the glob and yields the 8.x latest; `^8.1` has no wildcard segment and still yields the 8.x latest (correct for caret); `8.1.3` is still caught by the exact-version guard above; `~8.1.*` and `>=8.1.*` keep returning 8.1.

Extend the assertions in `tests/version-detection.fish`:

```fish
assert_eq (__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint '8.1.* || 8.2.*') 8.1 "compound MINOR pin -> first pin"
assert_eq (__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint '8.1.*@dev') 8.1 "stability suffix -> 8.1"
assert_eq (__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint '8.1.X') 8.1 "uppercase X wildcard -> 8.1"
assert_eq (__phpenv_parse_semver_constraint '8.*') 8.5 "bare major wildcard still -> series latest"
```

## Resolution
Replaced the end-anchored guard with an unanchored one that matches a MINOR pin anywhere and takes the first MAJOR.MINOR: string match -rq '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[*xX]' then (string match -r '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' -- $c)[1]. Verified across the full constraint table: 8.1.* / v8.1.* / 8.1.X / "8.1.* || 8.2.*" / 8.1.*@dev / ~8.1.* / >=8.1.* all now yield 8.1, while the deliberately-broad forms are unchanged — 8.* and 8.x still give the 8.x latest (8.5), ^8.1 still 8.5, >=8.2 still 8.2, ~8.2.0 still 8.2, 8.1.3 still 8.1 via the exact-version guard, 5.6.*/7.4.*/7.x unchanged. Five assertions added to tests/version-detection.fish, including one that pins the bare-major-wildcard behavior so a future widening of this guard cannot silently swallow "8.*" too. This completes the fix begun in audit-1f2c961c, which closed only the bare X.Y.* spelling.
title: MINOR pins inside compound or suffixed constraints still resolve to the series latest

## Problem

`__phpenv_provider_apt_get_php_path` runs `mkdir -p "$shim_dir"` before it checks whether the requested PHP version is installed. Asking for a version that does not exist therefore creates `~/.local/share/phpenv/shims` (or the XDG equivalent) and then returns 1. A lookup that fails should not mutate the filesystem.

## Evidence

`functions/phpenv.fish`, `__phpenv_provider_apt_get_php_path`:

```fish
    set -l shim_dir (__phpenv_get_shim_dir)

    # Ensure shim directory exists
    if not test -d "$shim_dir"
        mkdir -p "$shim_dir"
    end

    # Check if the PHP version is installed
    if not test -x "/usr/bin/php$phpenv_version"
        return 1
    end
```

The mkdir is unconditional and precedes the guard. Demonstrated by removing the directory and asking for a version that cannot exist:

```
$ rm -rf ~/.local/share/phpenv/shims
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish; __phpenv_set_php_path 99.99' ; # fails, as expected
$ test -d ~/.local/share/phpenv/shims && echo EXISTS
EXISTS
```

The directory is only ever populated further down, inside the symlink loop that the early `return 1` skips, so nothing needs it before the guard.

## Impact

`phpenv use <uninstalled-version>` and the auto-switch handler both reach this path on the failure route, so a directory appears in the user's data dir for a version manager that never successfully managed anything — including on machines using the homebrew provider, if `PHPENV_PROVIDER=apt` is set or auto-detection picks apt. `phpenv doctor` then reports `✓ Shim directory exists`, implying a working apt setup that does not exist. It also makes the failure path untestable without side effects: any test exercising a failed lookup writes outside its sandbox (see the companion finding on tests/path-management.fish).

## Fix

Move the mkdir below the installed-check, so it runs only when symlinks are about to be written:

```fish
    set -l shim_dir (__phpenv_get_shim_dir)

    # Check if the PHP version is installed
    if not test -x "/usr/bin/php$phpenv_version"
        return 1
    end

    # Create the shim dir only once there is something to put in it
    if not test -d "$shim_dir"
        mkdir -p "$shim_dir"
    end
```

Nothing between the two blocks reads `$shim_dir`, so the move is behavior-preserving on the success path. Add an assertion to `tests/path-management.fish` that a failed lookup leaves no directory behind, using a sandboxed `XDG_DATA_HOME` so the check is independent of the developer's real data dir.

## Resolution
Moved the mkdir below the installed-check in __phpenv_provider_apt_get_php_path, so the shim directory is created only when symlinks are about to be written. Nothing between the two blocks reads $shim_dir, so the success path is unchanged. Verified with a sandboxed XDG_DATA_HOME: __phpenv_set_php_path 99.99 exits 1 and leaves no phpenv/shims directory behind, where it previously created one. Regression assertion added to tests/path-management.fish.
title: A failed PHP path lookup still creates the shim directory on disk

## Problem

`tests/path-management.fish` calls `__phpenv_set_php_path 99.99` to assert the failure path, which reaches `__phpenv_provider_apt_get_php_path` and creates the real shim directory under `$XDG_DATA_HOME`/`~/.local/share`. Every other filesystem effect in the suite is confined to a `mktemp -d` sandbox; this one escapes it. The suite does not set `XDG_DATA_HOME`, so it inherits whatever the developer's shell has.

## Evidence

```
$ rm -rf ~/.local/share/phpenv/shims
$ test -d ~/.local/share/phpenv/shims && echo EXISTS || echo absent
absent
$ fish tests/path-management.fish >/dev/null 2>&1
$ test -d ~/.local/share/phpenv/shims && echo EXISTS || echo absent
EXISTS
```

The triggering assertion:

```fish
__phpenv_set_php_path 99.99 >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_fails $status "set_php_path: fails for a version that is not installed"
```

`__phpenv_get_shim_dir` resolves `$XDG_DATA_HOME/phpenv/shims`, else `~/.local/share/phpenv/shims`; neither is redirected by the suite.

## Impact

Running the tests litters the developer's data directory with a directory implying phpenv is configured for apt shims. `phpenv doctor` afterwards reports `✓ Shim directory exists: ...`, which is misleading on a machine that has never installed anything through phpenv. On CI the runner is ephemeral so nothing is observed, which is why it went unnoticed. It also means the suite is not reproducible in isolation: its behavior depends on the developer's `XDG_DATA_HOME`.

## Fix

Sandbox the data dir for the whole suite, near the top of `tests/path-management.fish` after the sources:

```fish
# Redirect the shim directory into the sandbox: __phpenv_get_shim_dir reads
# XDG_DATA_HOME, and the failure-path assertions below would otherwise create
# the real ~/.local/share/phpenv/shims on the developer's machine.
set -l xdg_sandbox (mktemp -d 2>/dev/null; or mktemp -d -t phpenv-xdg)
set -gx XDG_DATA_HOME $xdg_sandbox
```

and remove it at the end alongside the other cleanup:

```fish
set -e XDG_DATA_HOME
rm -rf $xdg_sandbox
```

With the companion fix to `__phpenv_provider_apt_get_php_path` (finding audit-6097be0b) the failed lookup stops creating the directory at all; keep the sandbox regardless, so a future assertion that exercises the *success* path also stays contained. Then add the regression assertion that finding calls for:

```fish
__phpenv_set_php_path 99.99 >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_fails $status "set_php_path: fails for a version that is not installed"
if test -d "$xdg_sandbox/phpenv/shims"
    echo "FAIL set_php_path: failed lookup created the shim directory"
    set -g test_failures (math $test_failures + 1)
else
    echo "ok   set_php_path: failed lookup leaves no shim directory"
end
```

## Resolution
tests/path-management.fish now points XDG_DATA_HOME at a mktemp -d sandbox for the whole suite and removes it at the end. Verified by deleting the real ~/.local/share/phpenv/shims, running the suite, and confirming it is still absent — it was created every run before. The sandbox is kept even though the companion fix (audit-6097be0b) stops the failure path creating the directory at all, so a future assertion exercising the success path also stays contained.
title: Test suite writes into the developer's real XDG data directory

## Problem

One assertion in `tests/path-management.fish` verifies the dispatcher's jq exemption list by grepping `functions/phpenv.fish` for a literal source line. It tests how the code is spelled, not what it does: a whitespace change, a reordering of the exempt commands, or splitting the condition across lines fails the test while the behavior is identical — and conversely, the assertion would still pass if the guard were made unreachable.

## Evidence

`tests/path-management.fish`:

```fish
if not grep -q 'contains -- "\$phpenv_cmd" doctor help -h --help ""' \
        $repo_root/functions/phpenv.fish
    echo "FAIL jq guard: exemption list changed; re-check which commands need jq"
```

No other assertion in any suite inspects source text; all 90 others exercise behavior. The behavior this stands in for — that jq-dependent commands are still refused when jq is absent — was verified manually in a symlink sandbox but is not portable to CI, which is why the grep was used as a substitute.

## Impact

A false failure on any reformat of that line, which trains contributors to edit the test to match the source rather than to ask what broke. It also gives false assurance: it cannot detect the failure mode it is named for, since the guard could be present in text yet bypassed by a change elsewhere in the dispatcher. Low severity because the suite is small and the line is stable, but it is the only assertion in the repo that would survive the code being wrong.

## Fix

Delete the assertion. It substitutes for a behavioral check that cannot run in CI, and a test that cannot fail for the right reason is worth less than the documented gap already recorded in the file's comment block:

```fish
# Ceiling: these run with jq present, so they prove the two commands are not
# gated, not that they behave correctly when jq is missing. ...
```

That comment already tells the next reader what is uncovered and why. If the exemption list is worth protecting, protect it behaviorally instead — construct a PATH from a temp directory of symlinks to `/usr/bin` minus `jq`, which is what verified the fix by hand:

```fish
set -l sandbox (mktemp -d)
for f in /usr/bin/*
    ln -s $f $sandbox/(basename $f) 2>/dev/null
end
rm -f $sandbox/jq
set -l out (env PATH=$sandbox fish --no-config -c "set -gx PATH $sandbox
    source $repo_root/functions/phpenv.fish
    phpenv doctor >/dev/null 2>&1; echo doctor=\$status
    phpenv versions >/dev/null 2>&1; echo versions=\$status")
rm -rf $sandbox
```

That is portable — it needs only `/usr/bin` and `ln` — but costs ~1300 symlinks per run, so weigh it against simply accepting the documented gap.

## Resolution
Deleted the grep-on-source assertion. It could not fail for the right reason — it tested how the guard was spelled, would break on any reformat, and would still pass if the guard were bypassed elsewhere. The documented ceiling in the file's comment block already tells the next reader that the jq assertions run with jq present and therefore prove only that doctor and help are not gated. The portable-but-expensive alternative sketched in the finding (a ~1300-symlink sandbox of /usr/bin minus jq) was not adopted; the absent-jq behavior remains verified by hand rather than in CI, which is now stated honestly rather than papered over by a test that looked like coverage.
title: jq-guard assertion greps the source text, coupling the test to formatting

## Problem

`tests/helpers.fish`, added this session to de-duplicate `assert_eq`, ships four assertions. `assert_ok` is called from nowhere. It was written speculatively alongside the three that are used, in the same session that deleted four unused provider helpers for exactly this reason.

## Evidence

Call sites across all three suites, excluding the definitions:

```
assert_eq      61
assert_status   5
assert_ok       0     <- dead on arrival
assert_fails    5
```

`assert_ok` as defined:

```fish
function assert_ok -a actual label
    if test "$actual" -eq 0
        echo "ok   $label"
    else
        echo "FAIL $label"
        ...
```

`assert_status <s> 0 <label>` already covers the same case and is the form the suites actually use.

## Impact

Small but self-inflicted: a shared helper file is the worst place for speculative API, because every future suite author reads it as the sanctioned vocabulary and may reach for the unused member, cementing it. It also undercuts the dead-code standard applied to `functions/phpenv.fish` in the same session — audit-09fff085 deleted four helpers on the argument that an unused function is a cost with no offsetting benefit.

## Fix

Delete `assert_ok` from `tests/helpers.fish`. `assert_status $status 0 "label"` expresses the same assertion and is already the established idiom.

While there, consider whether `assert_status` earns its place: it is a pure delegation to `assert_eq` with no added behavior. It does carry intent at the call site ("this value is an exit status"), and it has five real callers, so it is defensible — unlike `assert_ok`, which has none. Keep `assert_status`, drop `assert_ok`.

## Resolution
Deleted assert_ok from tests/helpers.fish; zero references remain in any suite. Kept assert_status, which has five real call sites and carries intent at the point of use even though it delegates to assert_eq. The helper file now holds exactly the three assertions the suites call.
title: assert_ok in the new shared helper has no call sites

## Problem

Tightening `config set default-extensions` to reject-and-return (finding audit-80455911, resolved this session) also made it reject values whose only fault is a leading or trailing space. `__phpenv_validate_extensions` anchors its regex at both ends and does not trim, so `"opcache xdebug "` is refused outright where it was previously stored. The resolution note on that finding claimed "nothing legitimate is lost — the regex admits any [a-zA-Z0-9_-] word"; that was true of the extension names and wrong about whitespace.

## Evidence

```
$ fish -c 'source functions/phpenv.fish
    for v in "opcache xdebug" "opcache xdebug " " opcache" "opcache  xdebug" "opcache,xdebug"
        set -g PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS keep
        __phpenv_config_set default-extensions "$v" >/dev/null 2>&1
        echo "  [$v] -> exit=$status stored=[$PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS]"; end'
  [opcache xdebug]   -> exit=0 stored=[opcache xdebug]
  [opcache xdebug ]  -> exit=1 stored=[keep]      <- trailing space refused
  [ opcache]         -> exit=1 stored=[keep]      <- leading space refused
  [opcache  xdebug]  -> exit=0 stored=[opcache  xdebug]
  [opcache,xdebug]   -> exit=1 stored=[keep]      <- correct, comma is a real error
```

`__phpenv_validate_extensions`:

```fish
if echo $phpenv_extensions_string | grep -qE '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+( +[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)*$'
```

Internal double spaces pass, so the regex is not consistently strict about spacing — only the ends are rejected.

## Impact

Minor friction, not breakage: a user who types `phpenv config set default-extensions "opcache xdebug "` gets `Invalid extension list` with a message about name syntax, which does not describe what is actually wrong. Pre-change the value was stored, so this is a behavior regression introduced this session — small, but it lands on the least-informative error message in the function. Rejecting the comma form is correct and should stay.

## Fix

Trim before validating, in `__phpenv_config_set`'s `default-extensions` branch:

```fish
        case default-extensions
            set phpenv_value (string trim -- "$phpenv_value")
            if not __phpenv_validate_extensions $phpenv_value
                echo "Invalid extension list: $phpenv_value"
                echo "Use a space-separated list of names ([a-zA-Z0-9_-])"
                return 1
            end
            set -g PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS $phpenv_value
```

`string trim` is fish's builtin and removes leading/trailing whitespace only, so the comma case still fails and internal spacing is untouched. Add to the assertions in `tests/version-detection.fish`:

```fish
__phpenv_config_set default-extensions 'opcache xdebug ' >/dev/null
assert_status $status 0 "config set default-extensions: trims surrounding whitespace"
assert_eq "$PHPENV_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS" "opcache xdebug" \
    "config set default-extensions: stores the trimmed value"
```

## Resolution
Added `set phpenv_value (string trim -- "$phpenv_value")` ahead of the validation in the default-extensions branch, and corrected the comment above it, which had repeated the same overclaim as the earlier resolution note ("no extension name it refuses is legitimate" — true of names, false of whitespace). Verified: "opcache xdebug " and " opcache" now succeed and store the trimmed value, while "opcache,xdebug" is still rejected and leaves the previous value untouched. Four assertions added to tests/version-detection.fish covering both the trim and the still-rejected comma separator.
title: default-extensions now rejects surrounding whitespace that was previously accepted
